newsitem.title: ITALY: Bertinotti says Italy government majority at risk.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti says Italy government majority at risk.

text.p: Italy's Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said after a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Thursday that the parliamentary majority supporting the centre-left government was "at risk."
"The majority is at risk and we have to settle the differences in order to keep this majority together," Bertinotti told reporters after the meeting.
Prodi relies upon Refoundation for a parliamentary majority and the two sides have had a strained relationship since Prodi took office in May 1996.
Bertinotti said he told Prodi that he was worried about the government's recent policies regarding privatisation, welfare reform, employment and fiscal evasion.
"The government's policies on privatisations just do not cut it," Bertinotti said.
Earlier on Thursday, opposition by the hard-left party prevented the Chamber of Deputies from giving a favourable opinion to a government decree for the privatisation of telecom group Telecom Italia.
Though the opinion would have been non-binding, it would have shown that the government's plans for the privatisation, set for mid-October, had parliamentary support.
Bertinotti also said he was worried about the development of talks underway between government, unions and employers on reforming Italy's costly welfare state.
"In these days, there has been no step forward on the welfare state front," Bertinotti said.
Prodi launched the talks in June, and from the beginning Bertinotti warned that he was against cuts in social spending.
The prickliest part of the discussions, reform of Italy's bloated pension spending, was postponed until September because it ran into rough waters this week.
"We have to find a convergence that will allow the majority to withstand the impact of the autumn," Bertinotti warned.
In April, Bertinotti's refusal to back the deployment of an Italian-led security force for Albania almost caused Prodi's government to fall.
